fatal_errors: The proposed Ti-6Al-4V polycrystal is unrelated to the target equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals.
The proposed tensile tests at 25–400 °C omit the target compression experiments spanning 9–1373 K, including cryogenic inertial dulling and high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier regimes.

The mechanism substitutes generic grain-boundary sliding for the target composition-dependent lattice-distortion strengthening, phonon-drag-controlled dislocation inertia, and Cottrell-type dynamic solute pinning.
The quantitative predictions of 30% greater plastic strain and 20% lower yield strength are unsupported by evidence.
No supporting or conflicting evidence is cited.
explanation: The hypothesis broadly recognizes that deformation in an alloy can depend on temperature and proposes a falsifiable mechanical test, but it does not reconstruct the target material, specimen state, loading mode, temperature range, strain-rate protocol, or CRSS analysis. Its expected monotonic thermal softening also misses the target's nearly doubled cryogenic CRSS, low-temperature inertial dulling, and elevated-temperature serrated strengthening peak. The generic thermally activated glide statement provides only limited mechanistic overlap. Although the Ti-6Al-4V experiment could independently investigate temperature-dependent deformation, the specific numerical claims and grain-boundary-sliding attribution are not supported, so it is not a well-evidenced alternative.
